ratings_why.fun: One shared pile and one keyword make a clear engine: bury tonight, everything with Fruit grows tomorrow, and Bootlace's run gives the board a shape to build toward.
ratings_why.distinct: A board-wide stat pile fed by deaths and drunk by Fruit plays unlike today's six tribes, though the death-text half leans on the familiar deathrattle tribe.

verdict_why: The engine reads well; two cards have wording a player can misread, and those are real fixes.

points.text: Moss-Bier Bearer's "it permanently gains +1/+1" reads as the dying unit gaining stats. Say "this permanently gains +1/+1".
Ludwig, the Lodger "gains its stats" doesn't say printed or current, and with White-Rot Renderer that is the whole difference. Name which one on the card.
Show the Compost as a pile with its quarter beside it, and Fruit as pips on each unit, so the overnight payout is readable before you end the turn.
While recruiting, mark Warden Amanita's two neighbours as doomed, so the sacrifice is visible on the board rather than remembered.
Rootbinder could also give Fruit to Spores beside it, so the mycorrhiza card still does something on a mostly-Guild board without losing its splash hook.

standouts.why: Grandmother Bootlace is the network made literal: an unbroken touching run all drinks from the pile, and your own burials cut it.
Clerk Inkcap writes each death twice and shrinks with every entry; the story is the rule.
Warden Amanita is the undertaker who caused the death, in one plain line, and it names the fight-side build.

weakest.why: Hired Mute is a generic gold condition; the silent mute at the gate doesn't show in what it does.
Moss-Bier Bearer is a stock grow-when-neighbours-die card with an unclear pronoun.
Rootbinder is blank on a Guild-only board, so it often reads as a vanilla 4/5.

flags.note: Golden Mourner of Three Rains keeps the whole pile, so every Fruit gains from a pile that only grows.
Guild Sealbearer stacked with Bootlace and goldens puts four or more Fruit on one carry.
Ludwig's "its stats" could mean printed or current.
Moss-Bier Bearer's "it" could mean the dying unit or this.
